name: Kumu Art Museum
known: The foundation's five-member supervisory board is appointed by the founder, the state, and elects the one-person management board (2023 activity report).
Art Museum of Estonia foundation, whose founder rights the Ministry of Culture exercises

name: Tallinn Art Hall (Tallinna Kunstihoone)
known: Paul Aguraiuja is the director (The Art Newspaper).
Estonian Wikipedia says he was chosen as director on 8 June 2020.
Ministry of Culture and Estonian Artists' Union, the founders

name: Zoma Museum
known: Co-founded by curator and anthropologist Meskerem Assegued and artist Elias Sime.
From 2013 the founders bought the land with Assegued's income as a curator and anthropologist and with sales of Sime's artwork (Artforum).
Privately funded; the founders were setting up a foundation to sustain it long term (The Reporter).

name: Listasavn Føroya (National Gallery of the Faroe Islands)
known: Karina Lykke Grand left the director's post on 1 April 2024; board chairman Niels Christian Nolsøe said she had secured funding for the modernisation of the museum (stated by the space).

name: Fiji Museum
known: Wikipedia states that its director Sipiriano Nemani opposed a 2019 proposal to let the Indian High Commission develop part of Thurston Gardens, and that in 2021 a corruption acquittal of former director Timaima Sagale Buadromo was reversed, pending a new trial.
Chief executive Armando Lowe said the museum still needs more funding beyond March 2027 (MAI TV, Lusi Banuve, "Preserving History One Artifact at a Time;

name: Oceania Centre for Arts, Culture and Pacific Studies (USP)
known: Founded in 1997 as a special project of the USP University Council, with Professor Epeli Hau'ofa as its first director (USP page, archived 2018).

name: Villa Skeppet
known: The Board of Trustees has six members: Alexander Bargum (chair), Jonas Lång (vice chair), Iris Andersson, Tuomas Heikkilä, Sophia Jansson and Christine Schildt.
Jennifer Dahlbäck is executive director.
A board of six trustees and an executive director are named on the site.

name: EMMA Espoo Museum of Modern Art
known: Saija Äikäs chairs the foundation's board (EMMA).

name: Gallen-Kallela Museum
known: Board and founders are listed on the foundation page.

name: Amos Rex
known: Director Kai Kartio said it was done "without recourse to taxpayers" (Museums Journal, 2019).

name: Didrichsen Art Museum
known: Art museum and sculpture park beside the founders' home at Kuusilahdenkuja 1 on Kuusisaari island, western Helsinki, by the sea.
Named for the founders.

Its by-laws, updated in 2019 "in conjunction with changes to the government transfer system of the Ministry of Education and Culture", require at least two founders' descendants on the board where available (stated by the foundation).

Transmeri is a family-owned company for beauty and everyday consumer goods, founded by Gunnar Didrichsen in 1928; its own page presents the museum as part of the company's history and does not call itself a sponsor.
The founders' home, designed by Viljo Revell and completed in 1957.

name: HIAP (Helsinki International Artist Programme)
known: Residencies last from 1 to 11 months for artists, curators and other cultural practitioners (hiap.fi/about).
The director is Emma Beverley.
The board for 2026 to 2027 is chaired by Vappu Renko of the Cupore Center for Cultural Policy Research (hiap.fi/about).

name: Kiasma Museum of Contemporary Art
known: One of three museums of the Finnish National Gallery, which falls under the Ministry of Education and Culture (stated by director Leevi Haapala in NO NIIN magazine).

name: MUU Helsinki Contemporary Art Centre
known: Governance: director Timo Soppela, chairperson Minka Heino and a seven-member board in 2026 (MUU website).

name: Siida Sámi Museum (Saamelaismuseo Siida)
known: Founded by Sámi Litto in 1959; runs the Skolt Sámi Heritage House and has cooperation agreements with the University of Lapland and the Sámi Education Institute.
